title.narrative: Support to World Bank/ EPAG Project Round 3 & 4

description.narrative: The World Bank (WB) Umbrella Facility for Gender Equality (UFGE) multi-donor trust fund is dedicated to advancing gender equality and women empowerment through experimentation and knowledge creation to help governments and the private sector focus policy and programs on scalable solutions with sustainable outcomes. The UFGE trust fund supports the Economic Empowerment for Adolescent Girls and Young Women (EPAG) program in Liberia. The overall objective of EPAG is to increase self and wage employment and earning among adolescent girls and boys as well as young women and men aged 16-24 years.
Economic empowerment of adolescent girls and young women, through business and job skills training

According to EPAG completion report, participants were overall more likely to be employed after the program than before, but the statistical significance of this outcome was limited to female participants. Female graduates who were not employed before the program were 18 times more likely to be employed after the program. On average, participants earned almost $20.00 per week more after the EPAG program. The percentage of young women who were unemployed at the beginning of the program (i.e., earning nothing) fell from almost 60% to under 4%. As a result of the intervention, all EPAG IV BDS trainees had created personal savings accounts with various banking institutions in the three counties of the intervention. An Alumni Network was formed to help young people that have benefited from the EPAG program to keep track of and support one another. Alumni networks were established in the five communities in the three counties of this intervention. Most beneficiaries spoken to during field visits expressed satisfaction with the program and extended appreciation to the Embassy of Sweden for the support. They see the program as relevant as it helps them to be self-reliant and provides opportunities for underprivileged youth to develop their skills. The team running each of the centers were seen highly motivated while discharging their duties.
